# C3. Other cost specifications {#esc-costs}

## A cost on the design {#esc-costs-design}

The paper's cost of redistribution scales with the size of the system and with the dispersion of relative incomes,
so it vanishes when the design redistributes nothing (appendix {{< var p.app_esc >}}). The alternative attaches the
cost to the design itself, $f(\theta) = \phi + (1-\phi)\theta^{p}$, with $\phi$ imposed and $p$ calibrated, as λ is,
so that the U.S. electorate re-elects its observed design. It charges a flat benefit whatever that benefit
redistributes. The table gives the two calibrations.

{{< include _generated/exhibits/ESC_CostCalibration.qmd >}}

Under the cost on the design, acute ageing raises the chosen design by less at every IES, since that cost does not
grow with the tax rate that ageing raises: by about half as much at an IES of one, the comparison the paper draws, by
much less at the lowest IES and by almost as much at the highest. France's voting
patterns move the design further toward flat benefits. France's income distribution compresses the redistributive
stakes but leaves the cost in place, and it takes the design to the Bismarckian corner at every IES.

::: {.oa-explorer .column-page}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
import {counterfactuals, control, ROWS_CHOSEN, RHO, CHOSEN_OUTCOMES} from "./assets/oa.js"
esc = FileAttachment("_generated/data/ESC_Counterfactuals.csv").csv({typed: true})
usObserved = esc.find(d => d.host === "US" && d.outcome === "theta" && d.reading === "pinned").baseline
viewof c3Out = control("radio", CHOSEN_OUTCOMES, {key: "outcome", label: "Outcome", value: "theta"})
counterfactuals(esc.filter(d => d.source === "main" && d.host === "US"),
  {rows: ROWS_CHOSEN, series: RHO, outcome: c3Out, mode: "chosen", width,
   observed: {"The paper's cost": usObserved, "A cost on the design": usObserved},
   facets: [{label: "The paper's cost", filter: d => d.spec === "size"},
            {label: "A cost on the design", filter: d => d.spec === "scale"}]})
```
